_comment: works-config.json の overrides の英語訳。キーはリポジトリ名。日本語版が正で、ここは差分の上書き。label / homepage / thumbnail / stack は訳す必要が無いので持たない。訳が無い作品は日本語のまま出る

kt-portfolio-site.thumbnailAlt: Portfolio hero screen showing KOKI TAKAHASHI at the centre of a ring of particles
kt-portfolio-site.description: A single-page site where scrolling carries you through particle fields rendered with React Three Fiber. There is one ring of particles per career entry, so adding a row to data/career.json adds another ring.
notes: Scroll position never enters React state — a mutable object is read straight from useFrame, so nothing re-renders and the scene holds 60fps.
Nothing external can break the build: the font is self-hosted, and if the blog RSS or the GitHub API fails to respond, the build carries on with the previously fetched JSON.

kt-tech.blog.thumbnailAlt: Tech blog home page with the headline "Where technology meets creativity" above a grid of post cards
kt-tech.blog.description: A tech blog that uses Notion as a headless CMS. Posts are written in Notion and everything else runs on its own: rendering through markdown-it, OG image generation, sitemap updates. Markdown, KaTeX and Mermaid are supported.
notes: Every page is served from the CDN through a Cloudflare Cache Rule with a 7-day TTL. On each deploy, GitHub Actions purges the cache and warms it again.
Post thumbnails are generated with the Gemini API, converted to WebP and stored in R2.

anoni.thumbnailAlt: The anoni home page: two characters alongside the tagline "a gentle space to share your everyday"
anoni.description: An app for sharing everyday life, where conversations with a character build up on their own as diary entries and memories. Built on the idea of "a gentle space to share your everyday" — somewhere set apart from other people's judgement and comparison. A live service.
notes: Subscription billing implemented with Stripe, with paying users on it today.
Next.js running on Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext, with Prisma + PostgreSQL and NextAuth v5 behind the auth and data layer.
A team of three shipped to production in about two months, and we have kept adding features monthly, working through 500+ issues and PRs together since.
For the memory feature, conversations are folded into a single diary entry per day before being embedded with pgvector, so past context can be pulled back in through RAG.
